items.question: Which older documented Erosion and TileGate behaviors remain exact in GAEA 2.3.0.1?
resolvedParts: Current official Erosion2 documentation explicitly describes deterministic results.
Current official tiled-build documentation confirms that some operations require nonlocal context and some current node pages explicitly require baking for Hybrid/Tiled builds.
Current official non-determinism documentation shows that deterministic operation does not imply cross-resolution identity.
items.remainingUnknown: A current official TileGate reference or exact current legacy TileGate semantics was not found in the bounded R02 search.
items.currentBestView: Use the current-doc-backed abstraction of an operator context/locality signature. Do not depend on the legacy TileGate node name or claim its exact behavior survives in 2.3.
items.promotionBlock: Blocks only claims about exact legacy TileGate implementation; does not block the general operator-context transfer.

items.question: Can seam blending ever be used in KAOPU runtime presentation without being mistaken for truth continuity?
items.reason: GAEA uses blending as an engineering workaround for tiled processing, while KAOPU requires explicit shared-edge truth contracts.
items.currentBestView: Presentation-only blending may be allowed later, but never as evidence that shared truth is continuous.

items.question: Does a deterministic operator imply identical output across different resolutions?
items.answer: No. Current GAEA documentation separately documents deterministic Erosion2 behavior and resolution-dependent procedural differences. KAOPU determinism must therefore be scoped to an evaluation contract, while cross-resolution equivalence is a separate property requiring separate evidence.

items.question: How much agreement between multiple external AIs is informative when their training/source overlap is unknown?
items.currentBestView: Treat agreement as a search signal only, not independent evidence.

items.question: How much measurable cross-resolution error reduction will footprint-aware field evaluation produce in current KAOPU and Mother implementations?
items.known: Primary sources strongly support filtering/sampling-footprint control as an anti-aliasing requirement, and a KAOPU-compatible plane-wave footprint probe has been authored.
items.remainingUnknown: The new probe has not yet produced a promoted runtime result and no Mother-domain fixture has compared current versus footprint-aware evaluation.
items.currentBestView: Keep evaluationFootprint/filterPolicy as Candidate contract fields; require an executed probe and Mother fixture before candidate-complete or Frozen promotion.

items.question: Can unified output normalization improve interchangeability without corrupting amplitude or energy semantics?
items.reason: Mature tools expose normalization for convenience, but normalization changes value range and can erase physically meaningful amplitude relationships if applied silently.
items.currentBestView: Normalization must be explicit, typed, versioned, and downstream-aware. Never normalize a physical or evidence-bearing quantity merely to make operator outputs look interchangeable.

items.question: Should stochastic procedural-noise evaluation be adopted as a general KAOPU acceleration method?
items.reason: NVIDIA 2023 research demonstrates value in Monte Carlo rendering, but that estimator context does not automatically transfer to deterministic world state, simulation, collision, hydrology, or evidence reconstruction.
items.currentBestView: Keep renderer-specific only until a relevant Mother proves unbiasedness, temporal stability, deterministic replay requirements, and task error under its own contract.

items.question: What is the minimum physically meaningful atmosphere state that KAOPU should preserve without overfitting UE or Karma parameter interfaces?
items.known: R01-R02 primary-source review supports explicit planet/reference frame, neutral thermodynamic/species state, separate aerosol/cloud media, emitter/surface coupling, spectral-property semantics, path query, evaluator policy, and camera/display separation. R03 executable evidence shows that one state can support multiple evaluators whose authority differs by query geometry; evaluator validity must therefore be explicit rather than global. R04 adds a multi-root Earth fixture architecture and shows that ReferenceSampleKey must preserve source-required context dimensions through reduction. R05 clarifies evidence class: NRLMSIS output is empirical inferred model state built from measurements plus constraints, not a raw Observation measurement. R05 also adds provenance-dependency and coverage semantics so fit/validation/retrieval status survives reduction.
items.remainingUnknown: The exact canonical Earth schema, state-source hierarchy above 86 km, required unit types, authoritative cross-root numerical fixtures, and the complete dependency/coverage graph for all candidate atmosphere data products remain unresolved.
items.currentBestView: Keep the layered Reference-State -> State-Reducer -> Runtime-Packet -> Evaluator architecture Candidate. Preserve independent Observation Root IDs, EvidenceClass, EvidenceDependencyDAG, per-variable coverage/support metadata, and a first-class ReferenceSampleKey. Require authoritative NRL numerical confirmation and authenticated spectral checkpoints before candidate-complete promotion.

items.question: Does KAOPU need a spectral reference layer for atmosphere, or is typed RGB coefficient storage sufficient for its intended world reconstruction and rendering tasks?
items.known: HITRAN provides wavelength-resolved molecular spectroscopy used for atmospheric transmission/emission, while modern atmosphere literature validates cheaper realtime approximations against higher-fidelity spectral references. NASA solar-irradiance material also shows strongly wavelength-dependent source and absorber behavior. This is sufficient to reject vendor RGB coefficients as the canonical definition of atmosphere spectrum. R04 further defines the minimum checkpoint metadata: spectral-coordinate convention, molecule/isotopologue, spectroscopy provenance, T/P, line-shape model, column/path state, units, and tolerance.
items.remainingUnknown: The wavelength domains, sampling/basis resolution, authenticated reference line subset, and task-specific RGB/few-band compression error budgets are not yet fixed.
items.currentBestView: Preserve spectral-reference capability and allow validated task-specific compression to RGB/few-band runtime packets. Do not require full spectral realtime evaluation by every Mother.

items.question: Should atmospheric refraction be included in the first KAOPU atmosphere core merely because it is an optical phenomenon?
items.answer: No. The reviewed current UE/Karma atmosphere cores are organized around participating-media scattering, absorption, extinction, transmittance, phase behavior, multiple scattering, and surface coupling. Refraction remains a real but separate process and should be added only when a concrete observable/process requires refractive-index gradients.

items.question: Where should KAOPU place the semantic boundary between neutral-atmosphere state and ionosphere/plasma/space-weather state for ground-to-space queries?
items.known: Current NRLMSIS is a neutral whole-atmosphere empirical model, while current NASA CCMC physics models such as GITM/TIE-GCM introduce ion/electron species, electrodynamics, winds and solar/geomagnetic forcing. NASA also notes there is no sharp atmosphere-to-space density boundary.
items.remainingUnknown: The smallest query contract that can couple neutral state to ionosphere/plasma effects without turning the first atmosphere core into a full space-weather simulator has not been defined or tested.
items.currentBestView: Keep ionosphere/plasma as a separate optional coupled state domain. Do not fake aurora, plasma or charged-particle physics by extending a neutral Rayleigh/Mie renderer.

items.question: Do the selected NRLMSIS 2.1 packaged test vectors reproduce exactly when executed from an authoritative NRL package or NASA CCMC host?
items.known: R04 inspected a non-authoritative mirror of the public NRL package. Its README identifies the same release structure and its legacy interface documents units and missing-value semantics. The mirrored expected-output file provides same-altitude 500 km vectors whose temperature spans 777.86-1116.07 K and total density spans 1.339e-16-1.034e-15 g/cm3 across different context tuples. R05 re-confirmed the official NRL release location and current NASA CCMC 2.1 host, but did not obtain an authoritative executable result.
items.remainingUnknown: The official NRL/Wiley binary release could not be materialized into the bounded R05 execution environment and the web-only CCMC interface could not be submitted programmatically, so no authoritative execution comparison was completed.
items.currentBestView: Keep those numerical vectors Candidate. Use them as a reproducibility target only; do not count the mirror as an independent Observation Root or promote the values until official-package or CCMC confirmation.

items.question: Which tiny authenticated HITRAN transition subset should become the first KAOPU optical regression fixture?
items.known: Official HITRAN documentation fixes spectral-coordinate and line-intensity semantics and shows that line shape depends on thermodynamic regime. R04 defines the checkpoint schema without inventing line values. R05 rechecked current HAPI documentation, which still requires an API key for data download.
items.remainingUnknown: No authenticated transition tuple was retrieved in R05.
items.currentBestView: Do not synthesize or copy unverified line constants. Retrieve two or three authenticated lines later and bind molecule/isotopologue, line provenance, temperature, pressure, line-shape model, column/path state, units, tolerance, EvidenceClass and dependency provenance.

items.question: How should KAOPU represent evidence independence when measurements, holdouts, empirical models and retrieval products share instruments, fitted data, retrieval models or upstream priors?
items.known: R05 primary sources show three distinct cases: holdout samples can remain in the same fitting instrument family; SCIAMACHY is external to the six NRLMSIS 2.1 NO fitting instrument families but its complete upstream retrieval dependency graph was not assessed; SABER NO adds a new sensor and full-local-time coverage but its concentration retrieval explicitly consumes NRLMSIS 2.1 temperature, O and O2. A four-axis executable probe demonstrates that a single independence boolean loses these distinctions.
items.remainingUnknown: Complete transitive dependency graphs, shared calibration/prior dependencies and quantitative correlation among all candidate atmosphere products are not yet mapped. The official NRL sample README also overlaps NO.15 between tuning and validation ranges, while the 2022 paper describes first 15 versus second 15 ensembles; exact file-15 membership remains unresolved.
items.currentBestView: Use EvidenceDependencyDAG plus multidimensional independence metadata. Keep sample-split, instrument/source, retrieval-model and shared-prior dependence distinct; Unknown edges stay Unknown. Root identity and independence must never be aliased.
items.promotionBlock: Blocks claims of independent corroboration where dependencies are unresolved; does not by itself block using a model as a clearly labeled empirical reference state.
